newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VENABLES SET TO TAKE AUSTRALIA TO FRANCE '98.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VENABLES SET TO TAKE AUSTRALIA TO FRANCE '98.

text.p: Former England coach Terry Venables confirmed on Tuesday that he had signed a 19-month contract as the new team boss of Australia.
He will coach the side in its attempt to reach the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
Under the terms of the reputed 200,000 pounds ($334,000) a year deal, a third more than he received from his England post, Venables will take up his new role on January 1.
He also disclosed that he would be moving up as chairman at English first division club Portsmouth where he has been acting as director of football.

The one-time Crystal Palace, QPR, Barcelona and Tottenham manager will spend around four months of the year in Australia with the rest of his time spent covering Europe keeping an eye on the growing number of Australian stars playing on the continent.
Asked whether he thought he could take Australia to the World Cup finals, Venables, 53, said: "I sincerely hope so, I wouldn't have taken it (the job) if I didn't think I could.
"That's got to be the target. I've got to work out how to get to the target, that's my job."

As it is, the Australians, whose only previous appearance in the finals was back in 1974, have what appears to be a relatively simple path with Oceania pool matches against the likes of Tahiti, New Zealand and the Solomon Islands. They must win the group to reach a play-off with the fourth team in Asia to reach the finals.
Bookmakers William Hill make them a 6-4 chance to qualify but a 150-1 shot to win the cup.
Concerned to deal with a number of legal cases pending, Venables stood down from the England post in June, after his side were a penalty shoot-out away from reaching the final of Euro 96.

He took up the part-time job as director of football at struggling Portsmouth and was linked with a number of big club management jobs both at home and abroad, including premier league side Blackburn Rovers.
He declined them all but could not resist the lure of the world stage which Australia offered.
"I think that what interested me was international football again. I've had two and a half years with England, and I really did enjoy it.
"I don't regret the decision that I made, after negotiations with the (English) F.A., but there was a frustration, and I would have liked to have finished the job properly to go to the World Cup.
"Now I have a chance to make that happen, and I'll do my damnedest to do that."

Ambitious Soccer Australia chairman David Hill could barely control his delight at finally persuading Venables to take the job, a week after it emerged that he headed the shortlist after long-term coach Eddie Thomson quit last month to join Japanese J-League side Hiroshima.

Hill said: "By our standards this is a big investment. We attach the highest possible priority to competing in the 1998 World Cup finals and for that we must have the best possible team, the best coach, the best leadership.
"Terry Venables is the best we could have hoped for, second to none. It's going to be a great adventure for him and for Australian soccer."

Hill also responded to the critical comments which have appeared in the press. Former national goalkeeper Jack Reilly had described the appointment as a disgrace and a slap in the face for the local game.

"The response has been overwhelmingly positive," he said. "Bear in mind that we have never had an Australian coach. The man Terry is replacing is Eddie Thomson who is from Aberdeen, he's Scottish. So if they can understand Eddie, then I don't think there will be much of a problem with Terry.
"I spoke to a lot of the players over the phone and every one of them was wildly excited about it. Venables is terrific for soccer in Australia."
Venables said: "You always get those for and against, I'll just do the best the best I can and go with the flow."
Venables' first assignment will come in January when Australia host a four-nation tournament against Norway, South Korea and New Zealand.
